tA.text: A · Two play modes: Time Attack and Classic (decided: direction A)

a_decided.text: Decided (#47, 2026-11-26): direction A. The mode is picked once, on the main menu, and the toolbar switches it from anywhere. Time Attack (cherry #ff3d55) keeps m4's map list and leaderboards; Classic (violet #8f7bff) gets a shelf of games. Direction B and its boards are removed. Each mode gets the screens that fit it, and the player card counts per mode (A11).

a_saves.text: Saves belong to the game (#851). Our UI never shows, picks or deletes save slots. Classic's Play opens the game's own title screen, and New game, Continue and its file select work exactly as made, so a port plays like the original without the original's exe. The shelf only reads the game's save files to show your progress (A4: stages reached, deaths, finished). A port without its own menus gets the standard engine menus in game pixels (A10, #100).

a_classic.text: Classic in a run: only the game and its art by default (A6). The session panel is a setting, off by default (A7). Pause is the new pause menu (D14): game time stops; Retry from save is what R does in the game; Back to the shelf loses progress since the last save point, as the game would. Leaving shows a session summary instead of results (A8, A9).

a_cost.text: Cost against today's shell. AppScreen gains Menu and Shelf; Select stays and becomes Time Attack's. The run already carries its PlayMode through PendingStart (#1544), so Run and its sub-states stay; RunScreen gains Summary for Classic. New: the toolbar, a mode accent token, the shelf (M; it reads the game's save files and writes none, so savefile needs no slot model; a game with three files keeps them as its own data), the main menu (M), the session summary (M), the pause menu (M). The two buttons of #1544 go away.

tB.text: B · The app shell: opening, main menu, toolbar, exit, web

b_flow.text: Start order. Every start: intro (B1, 1.8 s, any key skips) → main menu initial (B6). First start only: intro → notice (B2, #73) → setup (B3 language, B4 controls, B5 games) → main menu. The notice wording is a proposal; #73 (contacting Kayin) is still open, so the text says only what is true today.

b_menu.text: Main menu (osu!'s button system, our centrepiece): the delicious fruit stands in for the logo until #201; it bobs (1.6 s) and the wordmark under it reads the working title. Top level: Play, Browse, Replays, Settings, Exit. Play opens Time Attack, Classic and a faded Race (phase 8). The Classic button names the last game played; A on it opens the shelf with that game picked. Esc steps back a level; at the top it is Exit.

b_toolbar.text: Toolbar (B8). On every screen outside a run, 56 px at 1080p: mode switch, now playing, clock with session time, notifications, settings, you. No Home button: Back or Esc already steps back towards the main menu from every screen, and a Home button only duplicated it in the most valuable corner. The mode switch takes that corner. Controller: LB / RB switch modes from anywhere, Y opens settings, View opens notifications. Screens that are not a mode (Settings, Replays, Browse, Race) show their name where the switch was.

b_exit.text: Exit asks only when something would be lost or is still running (downloads, a queued clear); otherwise it closes at once. Holding Esc for 1 s on the main menu also exits, with a fill bar under the toolbar. The update prompt (B10) never shows during a run; it waits for a menu.

b_web.text: Web (#1127). The start screen exists because browsers keep audio off until a key, click or touch; it says that a controller press does not count, which is true today (web.md). Loading shows the phases the page already measures, so the bar is honest. Game select in the browser comes with #148; until then the page plays one package.

c_settings.text: Settings (C1–C5, #53): every row is a value settings.toml already holds or one #53 asks for (frame limit). Changes apply and save at once, like the existing hotkeys. Search filters rows across sections (C4). Online (C3): sign-out is #1491; export and delete are proposals that need server issues. Signed out, the Online section is the C17 sign-in card.

c_bind.text: Key bindings (C5, C6, #52). Client keys and game actions are separate groups, as in bindings.rs. Save state / Load state on F5 / F8 is a proposal for #39. A key already in use asks to swap (C5). Esc and Start show as fixed. Per game: the picker lists every game with its extra-action count; a game that needs an unbound extra action warns there and on the loading card (C8).

c_practice.text: Practice (C9, C10, #39). Three ways in: the Practice button in the Time Attack footer beside Mods (a sheet like the mod sheet), Practice this stage in the pause menu (D13), and Practise this stage on results (I2). Start from a stage, a save point or a room; the assists (HB, SS, SL, FA) are in the same sheet, and the run says Unranked everywhere. In the run the left column becomes the practice panel, with the death map and the consistency counter (I3).

c_misc.text: Details (C11) reads only #805 fields; brackets mark text that will come from the package or catalog. Collections (C12) is today's #105 feature in the Collections dropdown, with the heart on the wedge as the favourite toggle. Replays (C13, C14) list replays/index.txt and give today's viewer a face. Browse (C15) is the #50 catalog with removal-list games greyed. Profile (C16) keeps a slot for pp (#84) and shows milestones instead of badges (#489).

c_signin.text: Sign-in (C17–C19, #158, #159). One card with Google and Discord, then a waiting state while the system browser finishes, with the device-code fallback. An expired session toasts once and marks the toolbar avatar amber; queued clears wait. Decided: no outside reference site; the account pages and later the website (#85) are designed here, in this language.

tD.text: D · Redesigns: screens built without an artboard or marked revisit

d_answers.text: Decided (#47). #953 script error: changed as drawn (D1). #773 auto-retry: the mod select footer only, plus an AR mark in the HUD while it is on (D8). #554: Hitboxes is a practice aid, so a run with it is unranked; Flashlight joins Challenge as a ranked mod drawn by the client; Mirror comes later (#1574) and shows faded (D9). New on the same sheet: the Ghost switch (Off, Your PB, Board #1, #64), drawn only, so it never makes a board of its own.

d_pause.text: Pause, redesigned (D13–D16), replacing m4's pixel PAUSE box. Our own language: the game blurs behind, the menu on the left with the delicious fruit as the selector, and the right side used for what you want while paused: run time, the gap to your PB, deaths, the splits so far against your PB, deaths by room in this stage, and the game's controls (extra actions in amber). New items: Practice this stage (opens practice there, unranked) and Options (D15: only in-run-safe settings, nothing that touches the run). Time Attack says plainly that the timer keeps running; Classic says game time stopped. Restart run and Quit ask for a 0.6 s hold once the run is over a minute old.

d_notices.text: Notifications (D2, D3): one list, one look. Toasts: outside a run under the bell (top right); in a run at the bottom of the leaderboard column (today's place, kept). In a run only messages that need attention toast: storage problems, a controller change, a failed drop. Downloads, uploads, placements and updates go to the list quietly until the run ends. A toast shows 6 s; its thin bar counts down.

d_select.text: Game select gaps (D4–D7). Dropdowns open as a solid card under their control (the click-catcher stays). Group headers carry a status dot and a count. ListDim: the list dims to 50% while the left side (tabs, ranking rows) has the keyboard focus; Right or RB returns. Empty, no-results and loading keep the controls in place (D6). Status, Year and Tag filters wait for #805 data (D7).

d_kept.text: Kept as approved: the notice position in a run (the leaderboard column, #668), the results page hero (m4; Back now goes to select, D10, and a new block below it, I2) and the Unranked pill on the loading card. Changed since m4: the pause (D13–D16).

tI.text: I · New: built around how fangames are played

i_why.text: New ideas, from how fangames are actually played: a run is lost in one or two rooms, a jump is learnt over hundreds of tries, and the death count is half the fun, on stream most of all. So: race your PB as a ghost (I1, #64); results say where the time went and send you straight to practise it or watch someone faster (I2); practice shows where you die and whether a jump is learnt or just lucky (I3); and streaming gets first-class support (I4, I5). None of these touch the sim or a ranked run: they read replays, deaths and saves we already keep.

i_more.text: More ideas, not drawn yet: 1. Last death replay: in practice, a key shows the last 3 s before your death at half speed. 2. Sum of best and gold splits on the ranking tab (I2 mentions it). 3. A friend's ghost, picked from a leaderboard row. 4. A session goal ("clear Stage 4 today") on the shelf. 5. Room names from the package in the pause and death map, where the port declares them. Tell me which you want drawn.

tE.text: E · Cross-cutting: Steam Deck, Japanese, colourblind, sounds

e_pad.text: Controller-first (#117). Every screen has a hint bar showing the last device's glyphs (pad faces by position, or keycaps). Shared rules: A confirm, B back, X secondary (Mods, Details, Practice), Y favourite or settings, LB / RB mode or section, Start pause, View notifications. The Deck boards (E1–E3) lay out at 1600x1000 and scale by 0.8, so text stays readable; the player card hides there.

e_ja.text: Japanese (#196). The main menu (E4) and settings (E5) are drawn in Japanese with Noto Sans JP, the fallback the client already bundles. Labels fit at the same sizes; the longest (タイムアタック) fits the mode button and the toolbar. The Japanese strings are drafts for review, not final translations.

e_sounds.text: UI sounds (#488, no files yet): hover tick on buttons and list panels; select click on Enter or A; a lower click for back; mode switch (two notes rising for Time Attack, falling for Classic); dropdown open and close; toggle on and off; slider tick every 5%; notification chime (a lower one for errors); hold-to-confirm rising tone (release cancels); HUD pass and pace flash sting (off by default); results new-PB fanfare. All follow the Sound effects volume.

e_cb.text: Colourblind (#106, E6): every meaning colour has a second cue (a sign, the star, a word or a position). The pair to watch is green ahead and red behind, which merge for protan and deutan viewers; the + and − signs carry it, so they stay on every delta.

f_rough.text: Rough layouts for phase 8, only to check that the shell and HUD leave room. Race is a third mode on the main menu (faded today), with its own lobby (F1), a run where the left column becomes the race order and racers are ghosts in your room (F2), and a finish-order page (F3). Ghosts of leaderboard runs (#64) would use the same ghost drawing, picked from a leaderboard row.

f_data.text: Sample data: titles and creators come from our port list (creators we have not recorded show as [creator]). Every number, player name, save, music title, extra-action label and changelog line is invented, and brackets mark text that will come from the package or catalog. All art is placeholder except the delicious fruit, the real sprite uploaded to the canvas (not committed). The fidelity count in C11 (46 pass, 3 open) is today's kaenbyou baseline.
